commits.subject: docs: describe the desktop app the release actually ships
commits.body:
The README still described a repo with no desktop download and three
draggable borders in the desktop layout. Both changed: there are packaged
builds for Windows, macOS and Linux on every tag, and the chat pane now
fills the window with only the sidebar divider left to drag.

Also lists what each release carries, per platform, so the Download section
answers the question someone arrives with.

commits.subject: ci: fix linux deb packaging and dedupe release builds
commits.body:
electron-builder's deb target requires a homepage, an author email and a
linux maintainer, all of which package.json was missing, so the .deb half
of the linux packaging step aborted with 'Please specify project homepage'
after the AppImage had already built. Add the missing metadata.

Releases push the same commit to main and then tag it, which used to start
two identical 3-OS matrix builds minutes apart; the duplicate run doubles
the simultaneous runner demand (macOS runners are the bottleneck) and the
surplus jobs time out waiting for a hosted runner. Collapse them onto a
per-SHA concurrency group so the tag run supersedes the main-push one.

commits.subject: ci: name the repository when attaching release artifacts
commits.body:
The release job downloads artifacts and never checks the repository out, so
gh had no .git to read the remote from and the upload died with "fatal: not a
git repository" after all three desktop builds had succeeded. The wait step
already passed --repo; the upload now does too.

v2.9.0's artifacts were attached by hand from the same CI run, so the release
itself is complete.

Also correct the Linux filenames in the README: electron-builder normalises
the architecture per target, so the artifacts are linux-x86_64.AppImage and
linux-amd64.deb rather than the linux-x64 the table claimed.

commits.subject: ci: expire desktop build artifacts after a week
commits.body:
The artifacts exist to hand the three desktop builds to the release job that
runs minutes later. Keeping them the default 90 days leaves a second copy of
every build — around 800MB per release — sitting in Actions storage long after
the permanent copy is attached to the release itself.
